# Contributing

**Welcome to deepTools GitHub repository! Please check the following instructions
for contributing to the repository :**

## Adding features or fixing bugs

* Fork the repo
* Check out a feature or bug branch the you want to work on (for adding new
    features, use the develop branch)
* Add your changes
* Update README when needed
* Submit a pull request to upstream repo
* Add description of your changes
* Ensure tests are passing
* Ensure branch is mergable

## Testing

* Please make sure that github actions are passing

## Commit messages / PR titles

Releases are managed by [release-please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please),
which computes version bumps and changelog entries from
[Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/). PRs are squash-merged with
the commit message set to the PR title + the branch's individual commit messages, so
**the PR title itself must follow the Conventional Commits format** — that's the line
release-please actually parses:

```
<type>: <description>

feat: add --foo option to bamCoverage
fix: computeMatrix no longer crashes on empty bed files
docs: clarify --normalizeUsing options
test: add coverage for gzipped blacklist files
chore: bump ruff to 0.14
```

Common types: `feat` (new feature, bumps minor), `fix` (bug fix, bumps patch), `docs`,
`test`, `refactor`, `perf`, `chore`, `ci`. For a breaking change, add `!` after the type
in the PR title (e.g. `feat!: remove --exactScaling`) — this is what triggers a major
version bump, so use it deliberately. Prefer the `!` marker over a `BREAKING CHANGE:`
footer buried in one of the branch's individual commits, since the title is what's
guaranteed to be checked.

`CHANGELOG.md` from the `## 4.0.0` entry onward is generated by release-please's
release PRs — don't hand-edit those sections; anything above `## 4.0.0` gets
inserted automatically. Entries `## 4.0.0` and below are the pre-release-please
historical record and stay frozen.
